mainTopic: Offering blood on the day of slaughter, the night before the third day of a שלמים, and the rules of בכור, מעשר and פסח
overview: The amud opens at the end of a proof from the פסוק 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו' that the blood of a קרבן may only be offered on the day the animal was slaughtered. Two objections are answered the same way: whichever word you give another job, the other word is extra and teaches the rule. Then חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about the night before the third day of a שלמים. They disagree whether planning to eat it then makes it פיגול, and whether someone who eats it then is חייב כרת. A ברייתא is brought in support of רבי יוחנן. Another ברייתא uses פסוקים to teach that a two-day שלמים is eaten only until sunset of the second day, and that its leftovers are burned only by day on the third day. A new משנה then teaches that בכור, מעשר and פסח are slaughtered anywhere in the עזרה, need one blood placement that reaches the יסוד, and differ in how they are eaten. The גמרא says the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. It also learns the יסוד rule from a גזירה שוה with the עולה.

steps.title: The verse is needed for its plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: The end of an objection: the פסוק may only be teaching how long the meat may be eaten, not a rule about the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Say the verse is needed] for its own plain meaning!
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes a challenge that started just before this section. The challenger says the פסוק 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאכל' is simply teaching how long a שלמים may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wanted to learn from this פסוק that the blood must be offered on the day of slaughter. The objection is that the פסוק already has a job: setting the eating time of two days. If it has a plain job, we cannot squeeze an extra rule out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, meaning the פסוק is needed for its own plain message
A פסוק (verse)

steps.confusionAlert: This word is the END of a question that began earlier. Don't read it as a new statement. It is the objection the next step answers.

phrases.english: [It is needed] for itself!
phrases.notes: Meaning: the פסוק is just telling us the meat may be eaten that day and the next, nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an objection begun before this section against learning the blood rule from ביום הקריבו את זבחו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that blood may only be offered on the day of slaughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק has its own plain purpose, setting the eating time, so it is not free to teach an extra rule.

steps.title: The extra word 'הקריבו' teaches the blood rule
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant to set the eating time, it would have said 'ביום זבחו יאכל'. The added word 'הקריבו' teaches that offering must happen on the day of slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say: 'On the day of his slaughtering it shall be eaten.' Why do I need 'his offering'? Learn from it: on the day you slaughter, you offer. On a day you do not slaughter, you do not offer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The פסוק uses more words than it needs to set the eating time, and the extra word teaches the new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the eating time alone, 'on the day of his slaughtering' would be enough. Since the פסוק also says 'הקריבו' (his offering it), it is tying the offering of the blood to the day of slaughter. So the blood cannot be put on the מזבח on a later day, such as the following night.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces 'then the פסוק should have been written differently'
Why do I need it? Points to a word that seems extra
Learn from it; introduces the lesson drawn
Slaughter / offer (bringing the blood to the מזבח)

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
'On the day of his slaughtering it shall be eaten.'
Why do I need 'his offering'?
phrases.notes: The real פסוק (ויקרא 7:16) says 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו', with both words, so one looks extra.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
On the day that you slaughter, you offer;

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ אִי אַתָּה מַקְרִיב.
phrases.english: on a day that you do not slaughter, you do not offer.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק (ייתור לשון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only sets the two-day eating period.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'הקריבו' teaches that the blood must be offered on the day of slaughter.

steps.title: Maybe the eating time counts from when the blood is offered
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the פסוק means the two eating days start from whenever the blood is offered: today's blood allows today and tomorrow, and tomorrow's blood allows tomorrow and the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe this is what the תורה is saying: if the blood is offered today, the meat may be eaten today and tomorrow. If the blood is offered tomorrow, the meat may be eaten tomorrow and the day after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof again. It suggests a different reading of the word 'הקריבו' that does not forbid offering the blood on a later day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, 'הקריבו' is not extra. It tells us that the eating clock starts at the offering of the blood. That would even allow offering the blood the next day, the opposite of the rule just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; opens another possible reading
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Today, now
Tomorrow

phrases.english: But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
If the blood is offered today,
let the meat be eaten today and tomorrow;
if the blood is offered tomorrow,
let the meat be eaten tomorrow and the next day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2 by giving 'הקריבו' a different job.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'הקריבו' is an extra word teaching the blood rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'הקריבו' may be needed to say when the eating period starts, so it is not extra.

steps.title: The word 'זבחו' then becomes extra and teaches the rule
steps.stepSummary: If the eating time depended only on the offering, the פסוק would say 'ביום הקריבו יאכל'. The added word 'זבחו' ties the offering to the day of slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say: 'On the day of his offering it shall be eaten.' Why do I need 'his slaughtering'? Learn from it: on the day you slaughter, you offer it. On a day you do not slaughter, you do not offer it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way. Now the word 'זבחו' looks extra, so it must be teaching the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the challenger's reading, only 'הקריבו' would be needed. Since the פסוק mentions both slaughtering and offering, it links the two to the same day. Either way you read it, the conclusion holds: no offering of blood on a day after the slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: You offer it
His slaughtering (his זבח)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו' mentions both slaughtering and offering. Whichever word you try to use for something else, the other one is extra. Together they teach that the blood may only be offered on the day the animal was slaughtered.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
'On the day of his offering it shall be eaten.'
Why do I need 'his slaughtering'?
Learn from it:
On the day that you slaughter, you offer it;

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ אִי אַתָּה מַקְרִיבוֹ.
phrases.english: on a day that you do not slaughter, you do not offer it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by showing the other word is now extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק (ייתור לשון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eating period starts whenever the blood is offered, even on a later day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'זבחו' is extra on that reading, so the blood must be offered on the day of slaughter.

steps.title: Planning to eat a שלמים on the night before the third day
steps.stepSummary: Someone slaughters a שלמים planning to eat it on the night before the third day. חזקיה says the קרבן is valid. רבי יוחנן says it is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who plans [to eat the שלמים] on the night of the third day. חזקיה says it is valid. רבי יוחנן says it is disqualified. חזקיה says valid because it has not yet been moved to burning. רבי יוחנן says disqualified because it has already been pushed away from eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. Two אמוראים argue whether planning to eat a שלמים on the night before the third day makes it פיגול, a קרבן ruined by a plan to eat it too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים may be eaten for two days, and leftovers are burned on the third day. חזקיה says the night before the third day is not yet burning time, so the plan is not 'too late'. רבי יוחנן says eating ended when the second day ended, so planning to eat then is a plan to eat after the allowed time.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has an intention (מחשבה) while doing the עבודה
On the night of the third day (the night after the second day)
Valid / disqualified
Moved to the status of 'must be burned'
Pushed away from being eaten

steps.confusionAlert: 'אור' here does not mean daylight. It means the night, the evening that begins the third day.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who intends [to eat it] on the night of the third [day]:
phrases.notes: This is a שלמים, which may be eaten for two days. Leftovers are burned on the third day (ויקרא 19:6).

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya says: it is valid;
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is disqualified.
Ḥizkiyya says it is valid
because it has not yet been moved to [the status of] burning;
Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is disqualified
because it has already been pushed away from eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the night before the third day of a שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: valid, since burning time has not begun. רבי יוחנן: פסול, since eating time has ended.
steps.whyThisMatters: The argument comes down to one question: is the night in between still part of the eating time, or is it already 'after the time' even though burning has not started?

steps.title: Actually eating a שלמים on the night before the third day
steps.stepSummary: The same argument applies to someone who actually eats on that night. חזקיה says he is exempt from כרת for נותר. רבי יוחנן says he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats [the שלמים] on the night of the third day: חזקיה says he is exempt, because it has not been moved to burning. רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because it has been pushed away from eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the same two אמוראים arguing in a parallel case: actually eating the meat on that night, not just planning to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side uses the same reasoning as before. For חזקיה, the meat only becomes נותר when burning time arrives, so he is exempt. For רבי יוחנן, it is already past the eating time, so he is liable for eating נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: One who eats
Exempt / liable (here, regarding כרת)

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה looks at whether the meat has reached burning time. רבי יוחנן looks at whether eating time has ended. Each applies his view the same way to planning (פיגול) and to actually eating (נותר).

phrases.english: One who eats on the night of the third [day]:
Ḥizkiyya says: he is exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from the punishment of כרת for eating נותר, leftover meat past its time.

phrases.english: because it has not been moved to [the status of] burning;
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: he is liable,
because it has already been pushed away from eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same argument and reasoning from step 5 to the case of actual eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: exempt from כרת. רבי יוחנן: liable to כרת for eating on the night before the third day.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the time limits for disqualifying thoughts. For two-day קרבנות, planning to eat the meat after sunset of the second day disqualifies it, which matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רבי יוחנן. For קדשים eaten for one day: a disqualifying thought about the blood is planning it for after sunset. For the meat and the אימורין, it is planning them for after dawn. For קדשים eaten for two days and one night: for the blood, after sunset. For the אימורין, after dawn. For the meat, after sunset of the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יוחנן is right in his argument with חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that for two-day קרבנות, planning to eat the meat after sunset of the second day is a disqualifying thought. That means the night before the third day is already outside the eating time. This is exactly what רבי יוחנן said, against חזקיה, who held that such a plan does not disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Having a thought or plan while doing the עבודה, here a plan to do something after its proper time
The fat parts of the animal that are burned on the מזבח
Dawn, the first light of morning
Sunset

steps.whyThisMatters: It settles the step 5 argument in favor of רבי יוחנן: for a two-day שלמים, the eating time ends at sunset of the second day.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן:
Sacrifices that are eaten for one day:
a disqualifying plan for their blood is for after sunset,
and for their meat and their fats, it is for after dawn.

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אַחַת –
phrases.english: Sacrifices that are eaten for two days and one night:
a disqualifying plan for their blood is for after sunset,
for their fats, it is for after dawn,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִבְשָׂרָן מִשֶּׁתִּשְׁקַע הַחַמָּה שֶׁל שְׁנֵי יָמִים.
phrases.english: and for their meat, it is for after sunset of the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's side of the argument in steps 5–6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the night before the third day is outside the eating time of a שלמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that makes planning to eat the meat after sunset of the second day a disqualifying thought

steps.title: A logical argument that the meat may be eaten the night after day two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא suggests a comparison: one-day קרבנות may be eaten the night after their day, so two-day קרבנות should be eaten the night after their second day too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One might think the meat may be eaten on the night before the third day. And it seems logical: some קרבנות are eaten for one day, and some for two days. Just as the one-day ones get the night after their day, the two-day ones should also get the night after their days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea based on logic, and it is setting it up so it can be knocked down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A one-day קרבן, like a תודה, is eaten during its day and the night after it. The suggestion is that two-day קרבנות should work the same way, so they would also get the night after the second day. If that were true, eating on the night before the third day would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (opens an idea that will be rejected)
And it is a logical argument
On the night before the third day
The night follows their day

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a 'might have thought'. The ברייתא does not end up holding this, and the next step rejects it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One might think they may be eaten on the night before the third day?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two-day קרבנות, like a שלמים.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
some offerings are eaten for one day,
and some offerings are eaten for two days;

phrases.aramaic: מָה זְבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד – לַיְלָה אַחֲרֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: just as with offerings eaten for one day, the night comes after their day,

phrases.aramaic: אַף זְבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים – לַיְלָה אַחֲרֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: so too with offerings eaten for two days, the night should come after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same question, first raising the opposite logical idea.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the eating time of two-day קרבנות ends at sunset of the second day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparison to one-day קרבנות: since they include the night after their day, two-day קרבנות should too.

steps.title: The פסוק rules out eating on the night after day two
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והנותר עד יום' shows the meat is eaten only while it is still day, not on the night before the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And what is left until the day' — it is eaten while it is still day, and it is not eaten on the night before the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the logical argument from step 8 by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of what is left over 'until the day', and the ברייתא reads it as limiting eating to daytime of the second day. So the night after day two is not added on, unlike one-day קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a verse that settles the question)
Leftover קרבן meat whose eating time has passed
While it is still day

steps.whatToRemember: A two-day שלמים may be eaten only until sunset of the second day. The night after is not included.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches:
"And what is left until the day":
while it is still day, it is eaten,
and it is not eaten on the night before the third day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical comparison of step 8 with a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that two-day קרבנות may be eaten the night after the second day
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A logical comparison cannot stand against a פסוק that limits eating to daytime

steps.title: Maybe the leftover meat must be burned right away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that, like one-day קרבנות, the leftover meat of two-day קרבנות should be burned as soon as the eating time ends, which would be that same night.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the leftover meat should be burned right away. And it seems logical: some קרבנות are eaten for one day, and some for two days. Just as with one-day ones, burning comes right after the eating time, so too with two-day ones, burning should come right after the eating time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new 'might have thought' idea about when to burn the leftovers, and is setting up a rejection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the eating time ends at sunset of the second day, the question is when to burn the leftover meat. For one-day קרבנות, burning begins as soon as eating ends, in the morning. The suggestion is that two-day קרבנות should be burned as soon as eating ends too, which would mean at night right after the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the leftover קרבן meat
Right after, immediately following
Right away

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new question about burning, not about eating. Eating on that night was already ruled out in step 9.

phrases.english: One might think it should be burned right away?
phrases.notes: He means right when the second day ends, on that same night.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
some offerings are eaten for one day,
and some offerings are eaten for two days;

phrases.aramaic: מָה זְבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד – תֵּיכֶף לַאֲכִילָה שְׂרֵיפָה,
phrases.english: just as with offerings eaten for one day, burning comes right after the eating time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף זְבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים – תֵּיכֶף לַאֲכִילָה שְׂרֵיפָה.
phrases.english: so too with offerings eaten for two days, burning should come right after the eating time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 9's result and opens a new question about when the leftovers are burned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The timing of burning the leftover meat of a two-day קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparison to one-day קרבנות, where burning starts as soon as eating ends, so two-day leftovers would be burned that same night.

steps.title: Leftover meat is burned only by day
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק teaches that leftover meat is burned in the daytime, never at night. This blocks the suggestion that two-day קרבנות should be burned on the night after their second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'On the third day it shall be burned with fire.' You burn it by day, and you do not burn it at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge from step 10 by quoting a פסוק that says burning happens 'on the third day', meaning by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 argued that, like one-day קרבנות, the leftovers should be burned right when eating time ends, which would be that same night. The פסוק says burning is done by day only. So the leftovers wait for the daytime of the third day, and the comparison to one-day קרבנות does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (used to block a logical argument)
Burning (of disqualified or leftover meat)
Leftover meat of a קרבן after its eating time has ended

steps.whatToRemember: Two-day קרבנות are eaten for two days and the night between them. Leftovers are burned on the third day, by daylight, and not on the night before.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion about the night after the second day. It fits the view that this night is not a time for eating.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"On the third day, it shall be burned with fire"
By day you burn it,
and you do not burn it at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי בָּאֵשׁ יִשָּׂרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the logical comparison raised in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that leftovers of two-day קרבנות are burned on the night after the second day
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores the פסוק, which limits burning to daytime

steps.title: New משנה: slaughter and blood of בכור, מעשר and פסח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three קדשים קלים. They may be slaughtered anywhere in the עזרה, and their blood needs one placement that lands on the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The firstborn, the animal tithe and the פסח are offerings of lesser holiness. They may be slaughtered anywhere in the Temple courtyard. Their blood needs one placement, as long as the כהן puts it where it will reach the base of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out the shared rules for slaughtering בכור, מעשר and פסח and for placing their blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three are grouped together because they share the same basic rules. They need no special spot in the עזרה, and they need only one blood placement. The single condition is that the blood is placed where it can reach the יסוד of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, given to the כהן
Animal tithe (every tenth animal), eaten by the owner
Offerings of lesser holiness
A single placement of blood on the מזבח
The base of the מזבח

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The firstborn, the animal tithe, and the Pesach offering
are offerings of lesser sanctity.
Their slaughter is anywhere in the courtyard;
and their blood requires one placement,
provided that he places it opposite the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בכור, מעשר and פסח are slaughtered anywhere in the עזרה and need one blood placement that reaches the יסוד

steps.title: How each of the three is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה now shows where the three differ: who eats them, where, how they are cooked, and for how long. The פסח has many extra limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: They differ in how they are eaten. The firstborn is eaten by כהנים, and the tithe by any person. Both are eaten anywhere in the city, cooked any way, for two days and one night. The פסח is eaten only at night, only until midnight, only by those signed up for it, and only roasted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. After the rules the three share, it lists how they differ in eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור and מעשר have the same time limit (two days and one night) and the same place (all of ירושלים). They differ only in who may eat them. The פסח is much stricter: one night, until חצות, only for its מנויים, and only roasted.

keyTerms.meaning: The law changes regarding how they are eaten
For two days and the one night between them
Midnight
Those registered in advance to eat a specific פסח
Roasted over fire

steps.whatToRemember: All three are קדשים קלים and share the same slaughter and blood rules. The פסח stands apart in how it is eaten.

phrases.english: The law differs with regard to their eating.
The firstborn is eaten by the kohanim,
and the tithe by any person;
and they are eaten throughout the city,
prepared in any way,
for two days and one night.
The Pesach is eaten only at night,
and it is eaten only until midnight,
and it is eaten only by its registrants,
and it is eaten only roasted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from shared rules to differences
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בכור (for כהנים) and מעשר (for anyone) are eaten in all of ירושלים, cooked any way, for two days and one night. פסח is eaten only at night, until חצות, by its מנויים, and roasted.

steps.title: Which תנא taught this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows when it says all three need blood placement on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא of this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא's opinion this משנה follows. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה takes it for granted that בכור, מעשר and פסח all need their blood put on the מזבח. Only בכור is clearly written about in the פסוק, so the גמרא wants to know who extends this rule to all three.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who is the tanna?
phrases.notes: He is asking whose view says all three need their blood placed on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that בכור, מעשר and פסח all need blood placement on the מזבח

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא names רבי יוסי הגלילי as the author of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question and says the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב חסדא only gives a name. His proof comes in the next step, a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns this from a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: 'Their fat' and 'their blood' include all three
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the plural wording in the פסוק about בכור that מעשר and פסח also need blood placement and burning of אימורין on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, the verse does not say 'its fat' but 'their fat', and not 'its blood' but 'their blood'. This teaches that the firstborn, tithe and פסח all need their blood placed and their fats burned on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is talking about בכור, which is one animal, so we would expect the singular 'its'. The תורה writes the plural 'their', which tells רבי יוסי הגלילי to include the other similar קדשים קלים, מעשר and פסח. So all three need blood placement and their אימורין burned on the מזבח, just as the משנה assumes.

keyTerms.meaning: Their fat (plural)
Their blood (plural)
The parts of an animal burned on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. The plural 'their' in the פסוק about בכור brings in מעשר and פסח for blood placement and burning the אימורין.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
It does not say "its fat" but "their fat";
it does not say "its blood" but "their blood";
this teaches about the firstborn, the tithe, and the Pesach,
that they require placement of the blood
and of the sacrificial parts on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's answer with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the plural 'חלבם' and 'דמם' in במדבר 18:17

steps.title: Where do we learn the blood must land on the base?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the blood of these קדשים קלים must be placed over the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the blood must be placed facing the base of the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about another detail of the משנה: the blood must land where the מזבח has a יסוד. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 proved only that blood goes on the מזבח at all. The משנה said more: the blood must land on the part of the מזבח that has a יסוד. Now the גמרא wants a source for that extra detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The base, a ledge at the bottom of the מזבח
Facing, over, opposite
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Facing the base, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה from Step 12, which said the blood must land on the יסוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for blood on the מזבח was found, the גמרא now asks about the narrower detail of the יסוד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the blood of בכור, מעשר and פסח must land over the יסוד.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns it from the word 'sprinkling' by עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says it comes from a word-link: 'זריקה' here and 'זריקה' by the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: It is learned from the word 'sprinkling' here and the word 'sprinkling' by the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question. Because the same word 'זריקה' is used both for these offerings and for the עולה, the יסוד rule of the עולה carries over to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה, a link between two places that use the same word. The עולה's blood already needs to land over the יסוד. The shared word 'זריקה' moves that requirement over to the קדשים קלים.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, it is learned (used to bring in a word-link)
Sprinkling or throwing of the blood
Burnt offering
Learning one law from another because the same word is used in both

steps.whatToRemember: The blood of בכור, מעשר and פסח must land over the יסוד because the word 'זריקה' links them to the עולה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
It is learned from 'sprinkling'–'sprinkling' from the burnt offering.
phrases.notes: One 'sprinkling' is the word 'תזרק' in the בכור פסוק from Step 16; the other is the same word used for the עולה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'זריקה' carries the יסוד rule of the עולה over to these offerings.
